Key Finding: Interviews with 31 Brazilian young adults linked intentional searching and sharing of cooking content with established cooking routines; less experienced cooks compared recipes to build confidence.
APA Reference: de Camargo, A. M., Botelho, A. M., Dean, M., & Fiates, G. M. R. (2024). Cooking using social media: Young Brazilian adults' interaction and practices. British Food Journal, 126(4), 1405-1428. https://doi.org/10.1108/BFJ-07-2023-0607

Key Finding: Young adults valued cooking posts that were straightforward, trustworthy, novel, authentic, and tied to identifiable creators, while excess information felt overwhelming.
APA Reference: de Camargo, A. M., Botelho, A. M., Dean, M., & Fiates, G. M. R. (2024). Beyond catching a glimpse: Young adults' perceptions of social media cooking content. British Food Journal, 126(10), 3624-3643. https://doi.org/10.1108/BFJ-01-2024-0091

Key Finding: In a survey of 659 Pinterest-using parents, 26.9% read recipes daily, 17.9% shared them, and 13.8% reported making a found recipe daily.
APA Reference: Guidry, J. P. D., Miller, C. A., Hayes, R., Ksinan, A.J., Carlyle, K. E., & Fuemmeler, B. F. (2023). Reading, sharing, creating Pinterest recipes: Parental engagement and feeding behaviors. Appetite, 180, 106287. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2022.106287

Key Finding: The 2024 Philippine ICT survey found that 67.3% of people aged 10 and over used the internet, while 48.8% of households had internet access at home.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2025, July 21). 2024 National Information and Communications Technology Household Survey: Preliminary results. https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/nicths

Key Finding: The World Bank reports Philippine internet access remains sharply unequal by income: penetration reached 5% in the bottom wealth quintile versus 60% in the top quintile in 2022.
APA Reference: World Bank. (2025, July 2). Unlocking the Philippines' digital transformation by increasing internet connectivity. https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2025/07/02/unlocking-the-philippines-digital-transformation-by-increasing-internet-connectivity

Key Finding: WCAG 2.2 requires text alternatives for non-text content and names that describe the purpose of controls and input fields.
APA Reference: World Wide Web Consortium. (2023). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2. https://www.w3.org/TR/2023/REC-WCAG22-20231005/

Key Finding: Food and nonalcoholic beverages accounted for 40.9% of Filipino family expenditure in the preliminary 2023 Family Income and Expenditure Survey.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2024). 2023 Family Income and Expenditure Survey (Preliminary) [Infographic]. https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/infographics/2023%20FIES%20Infographics_0.pdf

Key Finding: Philippine year-on-year food inflation was 6.4% in October 2026, with rice prices up 20.7%, making ingredient affordability a changing household concern.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2026, November 5). Summary inflation report consumer price index (2018=100): October 2026. https://psa.gov.ph/content/summary-inflation-report-consumer-price-index-2018100-october-2026

Key Finding: The Philippine digital economy reached PHP 2.25 trillion, or 8.5% of GDP, in 2024, indicating a substantial national economic sector for digital services.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2025, April 29). Digital economy contributes 8.5 percent to the Philippine economy in 2024. https://psa.gov.ph/content/digital-economy-contributes-85-percent-philippine-economy-2024

Key Finding: UNEP estimated that consumers wasted 1.05 billion tonnes of food in 2022, with households responsible for 60% of the total.
APA Reference: United Nations Environment Programme. (2024). Food waste index report 2024. https://wedocs.unep.org/handle/20.500.11822/45230

Key Finding: FAO estimates food loss and waste contribute 8-10% of global greenhouse-gas emissions and also drive pollution, ecosystem degradation, and biodiversity loss.
APA Reference: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. (n.d.). Food loss and food waste. https://www.fao.org/policy-support/policy-themes/food-loss-and-food-waste

Key Finding: A Philippine household survey found rice was 58% of measured plate waste, with average household rice waste of about 49.6 grams.
APA Reference: Angeles-Agdeppa, I., Toledo, M. B., & Zamora, J. A. T. (2023). Does plate waste matter? A two-stage cluster survey to assess the household plate waste in the Philippines. BMC Public Health, 23, 17. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-022-14894-z

Key Finding: The Philippine Development Plan identifies unequal internet access as a barrier to safe and nutritious food access and calls for digital food marketing and delivery alongside waste reduction.
APA Reference: National Economic and Development Authority. (2023). Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028. https://pdp.neda.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Philippine-Development-Plan-2023-2028.pdf

Key Finding: The 2025 Konektadong Pinoy Act establishes a national framework for affordable, reliable, and inclusive internet access and narrowing the digital divide.
APA Reference: Republic Act No. 12234, Konektadong Pinoy Act. (2025). Supreme Court E-Library. https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/99600

Key Finding: The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition 2023-2028 establishes a six-year government strategy for national nutrition outcomes aligned with the country's development plan.
APA Reference: National Nutrition Council. (2023). Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) 2023-2028. https://nnc.gov.ph/plans-and-programs/philippine-plan-of-action-for-nutrition-ppan/

Key Finding: The Philippine Data Privacy Act requires personal-data processing to follow transparency, legitimate-purpose, and proportionality principles, with limits on retention.
APA Reference: Republic Act No. 10173, Data Privacy Act of 2012. (2012). Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines. https://officialgazette.gov.ph/2012/08/15/republic-act-no-10173/

Key Finding: The Philippine Intellectual Property Code protects original literary and artistic works, including photographs, from the moment they are created.
APA Reference: Republic Act No. 8293, Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. (1997). The Lawphil Project. https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8293_1997.html

Key Finding: The Internet Transactions Act covers specified business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions but expressly excludes online media content and consumer-to-consumer transactions.
APA Reference: Republic Act No. 11967, Internet Transactions Act of 2023. (2023). Supreme Court E-Library. https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/96902

Key Finding: A systematic review found that online nutrition information was generally of suboptimal quality and accuracy, and credibility cues can leave consumers at risk of misinformation.
APA Reference: Denniss, E., Lindberg, R., & McNaughton, S. A. (2023). Quality and accuracy of online nutrition-related information: A systematic review of content analysis studies. Public Health Nutrition, 26(7), 1345-1357. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1368980023000873

Key Finding: An Instagram analysis found 70.4% of sampled nutrition and dietetics posts were of none or very low quality; random hashtag searches did not reliably surface valuable information.
APA Reference: Kabata, P., Winniczuk-Kabata, D., Kabata, P. M., Jaskiewicz, J., & Polom, K. (2022). Can social media profiles be a reliable source of information on nutrition and dietetics? Healthcare, 10(2), 397. https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare10020397

Key Finding: A nutrition practice review describes how misinformation spreads through social media and emphasizes ethical communication and critical evaluation of evidence.
APA Reference: Diekman, C., Ryan, C. D., & Oliver, T. L. (2023). Misinformation and disinformation in food science and nutrition: Impact on practice. The Journal of Nutrition, 153(1), 3-9. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tjnut.2022.10.001
